text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The government is likely to announce a mini-budget after the cabinet meets on October 14 to approve a reform package agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
- Pakistan may sign an agreement with the World Bank this month for a $250 million loan to undertake the second phase of the Social Action Programme.
- Five major banks and development financial institutions have been directed to recover at least 20 percent of their bad debts by October 27.
- The government has decided to mend its fences with President Farooq Leghari by regularly sending ministers to brief him on the performance of their departments.

- A high-powered U.S. delegation headed by Assistant Secretary of Defence for International Affairs Franklin Kramer, is arriving on October 19 to take part in the Pakistan-U.S. defence Consultative Group meeting.
- Some armed men allegedly belonging to Marel tribe fired at provincial minister Inayatullah Khan Gandapur at Kulachi in North West Frontier Province. He escaped unhurt.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto has sent a special envoy to Central Asia to discuss developments in Afghanistan.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- Pakistan's foreign reserves fell to $856 million in September due to disinformation about the freezing of private forex accounts, resulting in an outflow of around $286 million, say sources in the Ministry of Finance.
- Telecommunication links with Kabul will be restored by Monday, Interior Minister Naseerullah Babar said. Telephone connections with big major Afghan cities are already operating.
- The new energy policy that offers a price of 6.5 cents to all producers could result in the power tariff being scaled up further by 112.6 percent by 1998, analysts say.
- The government is reported to have increased minimum prices of tobacco for 1996 crop by 10 percent.

- Germany, Pakistan's second-largest buyer of hand-knotted woven carpets, will stop importing from Pakistan from January 1, enforcing the Rug Mark System authenticating that the carpet being exported was not manufactured by child or forced labour.
- Three banks have asked the central bank's permission to open for business on Friday.
FINANCIAL POST
- The government is seeking feedback on crop insurance from insurance companies.
THE NATION
- The opposition alliance led by the Pakistan Muslim League has completed arrangements for today's anti-government rally in Lahore, the last in a series of protests around the country.
- President Farooq Leghari will embark on a three-nation trou of Central Asia from October 18. His 12-day journey will take him to Uzbekistan, Kyrygyzstan and Kazakhstan.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
